purpose: Baclofen is used to help relax stiff, tight, or spastic muscles. It is often prescribed for conditions like multiple sclerosis, spinal cord injuries, or other conditions that cause muscle spasms. It can help reduce pain and improve your ability to move more comfortably.
how_it_works: Baclofen works by acting on your spinal cord and brain to calm down the nerve signals that cause your muscles to tighten or spasm. Think of it like turning down the volume on overactive nerve signals that are telling your muscles to squeeze too hard. This helps your muscles relax and makes movement easier and less painful.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include feeling drowsy or sleepy, dizziness, weakness, and fatigue. Some people may also feel nauseous, have headaches, or feel a little unsteady on their feet. These effects are often worse when you first start taking it or when your dose is increased.
warnings: Do not stop taking baclofen suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause serious withdrawal symptoms like seizures, confusion, or hallucinations. Be very careful driving or operating machinery because this medication can make you drowsy. Avoid alcohol while taking baclofen as it can increase drowsiness. Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems, epilepsy, or mental health conditions before taking this medication.
typical_dosing: Baclofen is usually started at a low dose of 5 mg taken three times a day. Your doctor will slowly increase the dose every few days as needed, up to a typical range of 40 to 80 mg per day divided into doses. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribed and never adjust the dose on your own.
